title: Surrogate prediction API
card_detail: FastAPI service with validated inputs, uncertainty, tests, Dockerfile and CI file.
context: A small FastAPI service that serves the Gaussian-process surrogate with a 95 % interval. It shows the engineering around a model: input validation, batching, reproducible model versions, tests and container and CI files. Built in October 2026 as a practice project. It is not deployed to any cloud, and the Dockerfile and CI workflow were written but not built or run.

statement.tool: FastAPI, pydantic and a NumPy Gaussian process
statement.built: Four endpoints with strict validation, batch prediction, 14 httpx tests, a Dockerfile and a GitHub Actions workflow
statement.result: RMSE 0.82 degC on 300 unseen points; single request p50 1.0 ms in process; 4 of 4 invalid inputs rejected

flow_label: Request to validation to model to response
method_note: The model trains once in the application lifespan and is kept in memory, so a request costs only a prediction. The version is a hash of the training data, which makes responses traceable to a model.

plots.label: Latency
plots.alt: In-process request latency against batch size
plots.caption: Generated output · in-process latency, no network

spec: Ambient -10 to 35, EVs 0 to 250, shifted share 0 to 1, batch 1 to 100
Not deployed to cloud; Docker and CI files not yet run
decisions: Train at start-up for simplicity; a real service would load a stored model.
Reject unknown fields, so client typos fail loudly.
Measure latency in process and say so, rather than imply network figures.
verification: 14 tests through the FastAPI test client cover health, model info, accuracy against the simulator, monotonic behaviour, seven invalid-input cases, batch against single calls, batch limits and a reproducible model version.
